question: Türkiye is attempting to formally incorporate its so-called ‘Blue Homeland’ strategy into domestic law, promoting a policy that directly challenges the international law of the sea, the sovereign rights of the Republic of Cyprus and Greece, and stability in the Eastern Mediterranean.

This development constitutes a systematic effort to legitimise revisionist and expansionist claims against Member States of the European Union. Ankara is attempting to create a new fait accompli, ignoring the principles of international law. The European Union cannot remain idle in the face of actions against the sovereignty and sovereign rights of its Member States. Can the Commission therefore say: 1.
How does it view Türkiye’s latest attempt to institutionalise the ‘Blue Homeland’ strategy through its domestic legislation?
What specific measures does it intend to take to protect the sovereign rights of the Republic of Cyprus and Greece in the face of the ongoing Turkish provocations in the Eastern Mediterranean?
Does it intend to look into the possibility of political or diplomatic consequences for Türkiye?
answer: EN P-002111/2026 on behalf of the European Commission (19.6.2026) The European Commission follows closely the occurring media reports and statements referencing preparations for the submission to the Turkish parliament of draft legislation on maritime jurisdiction areas. The content of this legislation has not been made officially public. The Commission does not comment on media reports.

The EU has repeatedly made clear that Türkiye is expected to make an unequivocal commitment to good neighbourly relations, international agreements and the peaceful settlement of disputes. The EU remains committed to defending its interests and those of its Member States as well as to upholding regional stability.
In this context, the EU attaches the greatest importance to safeguarding the sovereign rights of all Member States, in full respect of international law.

Abstaining from unilateral actions, which violate international law and the sovereign rights of Member States, is an essential requirement to ensure a stable and secure environment in the Eastern Mediterranean and the development of a cooperative and mutually beneficial relationship between the EU and Türkiye.
